summary_paragraph: A pregnant patient with a history of bipolar disorder and prior psychiatric hospitalizations was admitted due to auditory hallucinations expressing fears about her baby's safety, consistent with a manic episode with psychotic features. She had no obstetric complications, and fetal monitoring remained reassuring throughout. She was restarted on haloperidol and lorazepam for agitation, with improvement in symptoms. Dehydration was identified and treated with IV fluids. Given her psychiatric history and ongoing risk, she was stabilized and transferred to an inpatient psychiatric facility for continued care. Her asthma and GERD were managed with routine medications, and she was discharged on a revised antipsychotic regimen with close follow-up planned.
